summary: Terminal list item lost after mobile background reconnect (SSE) — final bullet omitted on resume
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their mobile app (iOS/Android hybrid) backgrounds and later reconnects on a different network path (WiFi -> cellular), the SSE stream resumes but the final bullet points of a generated bulleted list are missing. Impact: Users observe truncated content at the end of long list outputs; manifests as last 1-3 bullet items missing or replaced by an incomplete final sentence. This is reproducible for medium-length streamed lists (~6-12 bullets) and seems limited to mobile background/reconnect scenarios behind the customer's corporate proxy.

Observed customer message: "When I reopen the app after switching to cellular, the AI reply stops one or two bullets early. The stream shows [CHOICE_END] but the last bullets never arrive. Refreshing sometimes shows them."
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start streaming generation from Redwood hosted API (SSE) in mobile app on WiFi.
2) While stream is running, background the app for ~5-20s (simulate OS suspend).
3) Switch device network from WiFi to cellular (or cause NAT/egress path change).
4) Bring app to foreground and allow mobile SDK to resume SSE connection using resume token header from client.
5) Observe that the stream completes according to client parser (terminal event received) but final 1-3 bullets are missing when reassembled.

comments: Support(Aisha): Initial triage - requested full client logs, SDK version, and sample prompt. Asked customer to attempt WebSocket fallback to determine whether issue is SSE-specific.
Customer(Grace, Noteable): Replied with SDK v1.8.2 logs and said WS fallback usually restores missing bullets but not reliably. Noticed problem happens more when corporate proxy is present.

Eng(Lina): Assigned for deeper investigation; running targeted trace in us-east-1 ingestion path and requested correlation IDs from customer. Added to priority queue for live debugging window 2026-03-14 13:00-15:00 UTC.
SRE(Marco): Noted increased RSTs on worker pool around the same timestamps and that some resume tokens were being rejected by edge due to stale session mapping TTL (cache mis-index).
investigation: Hypothesis A: Resume token mapping race - when client reconnects using resume token, edge may rebind to a different worker that has a truncated KV cache for that session leading to missing late tokens.
Hypothesis B: Proxy/coalescing on mobile path trims trailing newline/CRLF boundary; client parser treats stream as terminated (end event present) so no retry is attempted.
Hypothesis C: HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 gateway conversion (seen in logs) causes a half-close mid-chunk; server marks message complete before last bytes delivered to downstream.

Findings: Correlated customer stream ID resp_abc123 with edge trace; at resume the edge accepted resume_token but downstream connection reported WINDOW_UPDATE=0 during last kilobyte leading to internal buffer flush. Worker logs show final chunk appended but a subsequent connection-migrate caused reassembly map to drop trailing fragment (race in session reparenting).

Reproducer note: Team reproduced locally by forcing: (1) SSE stream with 8 bullets, (2) abrupt h2->h1 conversion via test gateway, (3) resume token replay — final 2 bullets dropped intermittently. Reproduced on serving-runtime branch: reproduce/sse-resume-handoff.
resolution: Workaround provided (2026-03-13): Advise customer to enable WebSocket fallback in SDK (SDK v1.8.3+ toggles ws-fallback:true) or increase client keepalive interval to avoid background session eviction. Provided feature flag command and sample client config snippet.

Temporary mitigation (server-side): Increased resume-token mapping TTL on edge to 120s and adjusted session reparent lock timeout to 250ms. Deployed to canary in us-east-1 (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4321) - reduced repro rate in canary tests.

Planned fix: Implement deterministic session handoff in serving-runtime (ensure trailing fragment flush and atomic reparent). Engineering RFC drafted; patch scheduled for v1.24.0 release (target: 2026-03-28).
Next steps: Keep ticket open until customer confirms WS fallback or server-side fix eliminates occurrences in prod. Postmortem to be created if recurrence after planned fix.
